assumptions: Subdomain of evidence_synthesis_and_systematic_review framed as session-bounded stepwise work units for the knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
No observed dataset or benchmark is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors for relative comparison.
Method definitions follow Borenstein et al. (2009) and the Cochrane Handbook (2019) as heuristic domain priors.
Scope centers on quantitative synthesis methods; qualitative synthesis is excluded.
exclusions: Primary study design and conduct (covered by research_design subdomain).
Domain-specific clinical interpretation beyond statistical certainty grading.

competency_questions.question: How is the meta-analytic question and eligibility protocol specified before synthesis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from PICO_PROTOCOL, SEARCH_RETRIEVAL, SCREEN_EXTRACT and workflow step 1

competency_questions.question: Which effect-size metric and variance derivation apply to each outcome type?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from EFFECT_SIZE scope and acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: When should a fixed-effect versus random-effects model and weighting be used?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from MODEL_CHOICE, WEIGHTING, POOL_ESTIMATE and CA_FIXED_VS_RANDOM

competency_questions.question: How is between-study heterogeneity quantified and interpreted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from HETEROGENEITY (Q, I-squared, tau-squared, prediction interval)

competency_questions.question: How do effect sizes, model choice, and heterogeneity jointly constrain pooling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from edges among EFFECT_SIZE, MODEL_CHOICE, HETEROGENEITY, POOL_ESTIMATE

competency_questions.question: How is the pooled result computed and presented without overstating certainty?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from POOL_ESTIMATE, FOREST_PLOT and CA_SIMPLE_FIGURE_VS_DISCLOSURE

competency_questions.question: How are sources of heterogeneity investigated while controlling multiplicity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from SUBGROUP, META_REGRESSION and EC_SUBGROUP_DREDGE

competency_questions.question: How is publication bias diagnosed, tested, and bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from PUB_BIAS_FUNNEL, PUB_BIAS_TESTS and EC_FEW_STUDY_FUNNEL

competency_questions.question: How is robustness to model, estimator, and influential-study choices tested?
When are network or individual-participant-data syntheses appropriate and what assumptions guard them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from NETWORK_MA, IPD_MA and CA_NETWORK_RANK_VS_COHERENCE

competency_questions.question: How are study selection, extraction, and quality appraisal kept reproducible and low-bias?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from SEARCH_RETRIEVAL, SCREEN_EXTRACT, RISK_OF_BIAS and workflow step 2

competency_questions.question: How is overall certainty in the body of evidence rated and communicated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from CERTAINTY_GRADE, PICO_PROTOCOL outcome hierarchy and FOREST_PLOT

competency_questions.question: How are cumulative and living meta-analyses updated without inflating false positives?
How is the entire synthesis packaged for independent reproduction and updating?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable from REPRO_PACKAGE and workflow step 9

glossary.definition: A standardized, comparable measure of the magnitude of an effect (e.g., SMD, Hedges g, OR, RR, correlation r).
A standardized mean difference with a small-sample correction factor applied to Cohen's d.
A model assuming one common true effect shared by all studies.
A model assuming study-specific true effects drawn from a distribution with variance tau-squared.
Weighting each study by the reciprocal of its effect-size variance.
The proportion of total variability across studies due to heterogeneity rather than chance.
The estimated variance of true effects across studies in a random-effects model.
An interval expected to contain the true effect of a new study, reflecting between-study dispersion.
A graphic showing each study's effect and CI, study weights, the pooled estimate, and heterogeneity.
A scatter of effect size against precision used to inspect small-study effects.
A regression test for funnel-plot asymmetry as an indicator of small-study effects.
A method imputing hypothetically missing studies to estimate a bias-adjusted effect.
An analysis of the distribution of significant p-values to assess evidential value and selective reporting.
Regression of study-level effect size on study-level covariates with residual heterogeneity.
Comparison of pooled effects across categorical study-level groups.
Joint synthesis of multiple treatments using direct and indirect comparisons.
The assumption that effect modifiers are balanced across comparisons so indirect comparison is valid.
Synthesis using individual participant data harmonized across studies.
A framework rating certainty in a body of evidence across five domains.
An appraisal of the internal validity of an individual study (e.g., RoB 2, ROBINS-I).

evidence_label_policy.rule: All values are heuristic priors; observed/experimentally_validated labels are disallowed because no dataset or benchmark was supplied.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established meta-analysis methodology (Borenstein et al. 2009 Introduction to Meta-Analysis; Higgins et al. 2019 Cochrane Handbook) used as expert-domain defaults, not measured data.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Borenstein, Hedges, Higgins & Rothstein (2009); Higgins et al., Cochrane Handbook (2019)
grounding_limits: values are heuristic priors for relative comparison only

nodes.definition: Specify the meta-analytic question and a pre-registered protocol with PICO/eligibility, planned models, and outcomes before any synthesis.
contradictors: post-hoc meta-analyst who fixes the question to the available data

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: protocol amended after data extraction begins or scope creep is detected

pros.claim: Pre-specification blocks data-driven outcome and model selection that inflates false positives.
pros.example: registering random-effects + I-squared plan before extracting trial data

cons.claim: Over-rigid protocols can miss legitimately important post-hoc subgroups.
cons.example: a strong dose-response signal not pre-specified

failure_modes: question reframed to fit retrieved studies
acceptance_tests: protocol exists and is timestamped before extraction
every reported outcome maps to a protocol entry or a logged amendment

nodes.definition: Run a reproducible multi-database search with documented strings, grey literature, and deduplication to assemble the candidate study pool.
contradictors: single-database convenience searcher

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new relevant database or missed seminal study is discovered

pros.claim: Comprehensive retrieval reduces selection bias that no statistical model can correct downstream.
pros.example: adding trial registries and grey literature to catch unpublished nulls

cons.claim: Exhaustive searching is costly and inflates screening burden.
cons.example: thousands of low-precision hits per added database

nodes.definition: Dual-screen records against eligibility and extract outcome, design, and moderator data into a structured coded dataset.
contradictors: single-reviewer extractor without adjudication

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: extraction error rate or inter-rater disagreement exceeds tolerance

pros.claim: Dual extraction with adjudication suppresses transcription and unit errors that bias pooled estimates.
pros.example: two coders independently extracting means and SDs then reconciling

cons.claim: Dual coding doubles labor and slows the pipeline.
cons.example: large evidence base with hundreds of full texts

acceptance_tests: pooled result and its limitations independently checked before finalization

nodes.definition: Choose and compute a comparable effect-size metric (SMD/Hedges g, OR/RR, correlation r) with its variance from each study's reported statistics.

included: metric choice (SMD, Hedges g, OR, RR, r)

contradictors: analyst who mixes incomparable raw metrics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a study's reported statistics force a different variance derivation than assumed

pros.claim: A single comparable, bias-corrected metric is the precondition for any valid pooling.
pros.example: converting all continuous outcomes to Hedges g with small-sample correction

cons.claim: Metric conversions propagate assumption error when primary statistics are incomplete.
cons.example: imputing SDs from p-values when CIs are absent

acceptance_tests: each effect size has a finite, correctly-signed variance
metric and correction match the outcome type

nodes.definition: Decide between fixed-effect and random-effects models based on the inferential target and expected between-study heterogeneity, and justify it.
contradictors: analyst who defaults to fixed-effect to get tighter CIs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed heterogeneity contradicts the model's homogeneity assumption

pros.claim: Matching model to inference target prevents overstated precision from a misapplied fixed-effect assumption.
pros.example: using random-effects when generalizing beyond the included studies

cons.claim: Random-effects can over-weight small, low-quality studies relative to fixed-effect.
cons.example: a tiny imprecise trial gaining influence under random-effects weighting

failure_modes: model not justified against inference target
acceptance_tests: model choice is justified against the stated inference target
sensitivity to alternate model is reported

nodes.definition: Assign study weights via inverse-variance (and tau-squared-adjusted) schemes, or robust alternatives, to combine effects.
contradictors: analyst using sample-size weights ignoring variance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sparse or rare-event data make inverse-variance weights unstable

pros.claim: Inverse-variance weighting is the statistically efficient default under correct variances.
pros.example: large balanced trials dominating the pooled estimate appropriately

cons.claim: Inverse-variance weights mislead with rare events and zero cells.
cons.example: 2x2 tables with zero events needing Mantel-Haenszel or Peto

nodes.definition: Quantify and interpret between-study heterogeneity using Q, I-squared, tau-squared, and prediction intervals rather than a single point estimate.
contradictors: analyst who reports only I-squared as if it measured amount

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: I-squared is misread as amount of heterogeneity instead of proportion of variance

pros.claim: Prediction intervals communicate the dispersion of true effects that a pooled mean and I-squared hide.
pros.example: reporting a 95% prediction interval that crosses null despite a significant mean

cons.claim: I-squared depends on within-study precision and can be near zero with few studies despite real tau-squared.
cons.example: low I-squared in a 4-study analysis masking real between-study variance

acceptance_tests: pooled result and its limitations independently checked before finalization

nodes.definition: Compute the pooled effect, its confidence interval, and small-sample-adjusted inference (e.g., Knapp-Hartung) under the chosen model.
contradictors: analyst reporting naive Wald CIs with few studies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: few-study random-effects CIs are anti-conservative without HKSJ adjustment

pros.claim: Knapp-Hartung adjustment restores nominal coverage when the number of studies is small.
pros.example: widening a 5-study random-effects CI to avoid a spurious significant result

cons.claim: Back-transformation and adjustment choices can change the headline conclusion.
cons.example: log-OR pooled then exponentiated shifting the point estimate interpretation

nodes.definition: Produce a forest plot and tabular summary that faithfully display per-study effects, weights, pooled estimate, and heterogeneity.
contradictors: analyst who hides heterogeneity behind a clean diamond

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: readers misread the diamond as the only result and miss heterogeneity

pros.claim: A correct forest plot makes the evidence base and its dispersion auditable at a glance.
pros.example: displaying the prediction interval alongside the pooled diamond

cons.claim: Polished plots can imply more certainty than the data support.
cons.example: narrow CI diamond drawn over wildly scattered study estimates

nodes.definition: Test whether pre-specified study-level categorical moderators explain heterogeneity via between-subgroup tests.
contradictors: analyst data-dredging subgroups post hoc

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: subgroup differences are claimed from underpowered post-hoc splits

pros.claim: Pre-specified subgroups can legitimately localize where an effect holds.
pros.example: showing efficacy only in adults via a planned age subgroup

cons.claim: Subgroup analyses are underpowered and prone to false positives when multiplied.
cons.example: ten exploratory subgroups yielding one spurious significant difference

acceptance_tests: pooled result and its limitations independently checked before finalization

nodes.definition: Model the relationship between study-level covariates and effect size using (mixed-effects) meta-regression with appropriate residual heterogeneity.
contradictors: analyst fitting many covariates to few studies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: too few studies per covariate produce overfitted, non-replicable coefficients

pros.claim: Meta-regression quantifies dose-response and continuous moderator effects subgroups cannot.
pros.example: relating effect size to mean baseline severity across trials

cons.claim: Aggregation/ecological bias and overfitting threaten study-level regression.
cons.example: inferring individual modification from study-mean covariates

acceptance_tests: pooled result and its limitations independently checked before finalization

nodes.definition: Diagnose small-study effects and potential publication bias visually with funnel plots and contour-enhanced variants.
contradictors: analyst equating any asymmetry with publication bias

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: funnel asymmetry is attributed to publication bias when heterogeneity explains it

pros.claim: Contour-enhanced funnels separate significance-driven gaps from benign asymmetry.
pros.example: missing studies falling in the non-significant contour region

cons.claim: Funnel plots are unreliable and subjective with fewer than ten studies.
cons.example: reading asymmetry into a 6-study funnel

nodes.definition: Apply formal small-study/publication-bias tests and correction methods (Egger, trim-and-fill, p-curve, selection models) and bound their impact.
contradictors: analyst trusting trim-and-fill as a definitive correction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a single correction method's adjusted estimate is reported as the truth

pros.claim: Triangulating multiple bias methods bounds how much unpublished evidence could change conclusions.
pros.example: p-curve and selection models agreeing the effect survives correction

cons.claim: Each correction has failure modes; methods disagree under heterogeneity.
cons.example: trim-and-fill over-correcting when asymmetry is from heterogeneity

acceptance_tests: at least two complementary bias methods are reported
corrected estimate is given as a range not a point

nodes.definition: Test robustness of the pooled result to model, estimator, inclusion, and assumption choices through pre-planned and ad hoc variations.
contradictors: analyst reporting only the most favorable specification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the conclusion flips across reasonable specifications but only one is reported

pros.claim: Sensitivity analysis distinguishes a robust finding from a specification artifact.
pros.example: showing the effect persists whether DL or REML tau-squared is used

cons.claim: Unbounded specification searching can become a fishing expedition.
cons.example: running dozens of specifications to find one significant result

acceptance_tests: pooled result and its limitations independently checked before finalization

nodes.definition: Identify outlying and influential studies (leave-one-out, Baujat, Cook's distance) and assess their leverage on the pooled estimate.
contradictors: analyst deleting inconvenient studies as outliers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an influential study is removed for convenience rather than justified reason

pros.claim: Influence diagnostics reveal when one study drives the entire result.
pros.example: leave-one-out showing significance vanishes without a single trial

cons.claim: Outlier deletion without rationale biases the estimate toward the analyst's expectation.
cons.example: trimming the only null study as an outlier

nodes.definition: Synthesize multiple treatments or correlated outcomes jointly, enforcing consistency and modeling within-comparison correlation.
contradictors: analyst ranking treatments by SUCRA ignoring incoherence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: transitivity is violated yet indirect evidence is pooled as if valid

pros.claim: Network synthesis uses indirect evidence to compare treatments never tested head-to-head.
pros.example: ranking three drugs from a connected trial network

cons.claim: Incoherence and transitivity violations invalidate rankings and are easy to overlook.
cons.example: SUCRA ranks driven by a single sparse indirect loop

acceptance_tests: transitivity and consistency are assessed before any ranking is reported
node-splitting shows no material incoherence

nodes.definition: Obtain and harmonize individual-level data across studies to enable within-study interactions and consistent re-analysis.
contradictors: analyst inferring individual modifiers from aggregate data

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: available IPD is a non-random subset risking availability bias

pros.claim: IPD enables valid individual-level interaction estimates aggregate data cannot support.
pros.example: testing whether treatment effect varies with patient age within trials

cons.claim: IPD is costly, slow, and partial retrieval introduces availability bias.
cons.example: only half the trials sharing data, skewing the synthesis

acceptance_tests: within-study and across-study effects are estimated separately to avoid aggregation bias
harmonization is documented and reversible

nodes.definition: Appraise internal validity of each included study with a structured tool (RoB 2, ROBINS-I) and incorporate it into synthesis weighting or stratification.

included: not converting RoB to numeric weights naively

contradictors: analyst ignoring study quality in pooling

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: high-risk studies dominate the pooled estimate without a quality-stratified check

pros.claim: Bias appraisal prevents flawed studies from masquerading as strong evidence in the pool.
pros.example: downgrading confidence when most weight comes from high-risk trials

cons.claim: Quality scores converted to weights can introduce arbitrary, non-validated adjustments.
cons.example: multiplying weights by a composite quality score

acceptance_tests: a quality-stratified or sensitivity analysis excludes high-risk studies
RoB judgments are at the domain level not a single score

nodes.definition: Rate overall certainty in the body of evidence (GRADE) across imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, risk of bias, and publication bias.
contradictors: analyst presenting a pooled p-value as certainty

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a statistically significant pooled effect is graded high certainty despite serious limitations

pros.claim: GRADE forces certainty claims to reflect all weaknesses, not just statistical significance.
pros.example: downgrading to low certainty for imprecision plus inconsistency

cons.claim: GRADE judgments are partly subjective and can be applied inconsistently.
cons.example: two reviewers reaching different certainty ratings on the same evidence

acceptance_tests: each downgrade/upgrade decision has an explicit logged rationale
certainty reflects all five GRADE domains

nodes.definition: Order evidence chronologically and update synthesis as new studies arrive, controlling for multiple-looks inflation in living reviews.
contradictors: analyst re-testing significance at every new study without adjustment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repeated significance testing as studies accrue inflates false-positive risk

pros.claim: Cumulative analysis shows when evidence became conclusive and reduces research waste.
pros.example: cumulative plot revealing the effect was established years before the latest trials

cons.claim: Naive repeated testing in living reviews inflates type-I error.
cons.example: declaring significance at the first crossing without sequential adjustment

nodes.definition: Bundle data, code, model specifications, and PRISMA reporting into a versioned, re-runnable package supporting independent replication.
contradictors: analyst delivering a spreadsheet without code or provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a result cannot be reproduced from the archived materials

pros.claim: A re-runnable package makes every analytic choice auditable and the synthesis updatable.
pros.example: a reviewer reproducing the pooled estimate from the archived script and data

cons.claim: Packaging and documentation add effort late in a deadline-pressured project.
cons.example: cleaning code and writing the README after analysis is done

edges.why_related: Eligibility and PICO defined in the protocol bound what the search must retrieve.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Search scoped to the registered question avoids irrelevant or biased retrieval.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Mild tension when the search reveals the question was too narrow.
edges.example: PICO terms seed the database search string.
edges.resolution_rule: Protocol dominates; widen via a logged amendment, not silent drift.

edges.why_related: Pre-specified subgroups in the protocol limit which subgroup tests are confirmatory.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Confirmatory subgroups gain credibility; post-hoc ones are flagged exploratory.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when an unplanned but important subgroup emerges.
edges.example: Only the planned age and severity subgroups are confirmatory.
edges.resolution_rule: Protocol bounds confirmatory claims; post-hoc subgroups are labeled exploratory.

edges.why_related: The retrieved candidate set is the input the screening and extraction step operates on.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Complete retrieval feeds complete, unbiased screening.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Minor tension over screening burden from broad retrieval.
edges.example: PRISMA candidate set handed to dual screeners.
edges.resolution_rule: Screening proceeds only on the documented retrieval set.

edges.why_related: Extracted study statistics are the raw material for effect-size computation.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Clean extraction yields correct effect sizes and variances.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when extraction omits the statistics a metric needs.
edges.example: Means, SDs, and n feeding Hedges g computation.
edges.resolution_rule: Effect sizes computed only from verified extracted statistics.

edges.why_related: The coded study dataset is the object risk-of-bias appraisal is applied to.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Appraisal aligned to coded studies enables quality-aware synthesis.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Minor tension over appraisal effort per study.
edges.example: Each extracted trial scored with RoB 2 domains.
edges.resolution_rule: Appraise the same study set that was extracted.

edges.why_related: The set of computed effect sizes and their spread informs the model decision.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Knowing the effects lets the model match the inference target.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when effects suggest pooling is inappropriate.
edges.example: Wide scatter of effects steering toward random-effects.
edges.resolution_rule: Model chosen after effects are computed, justified to inference target.

edges.why_related: Per-study effects and variances are required inputs to heterogeneity statistics.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Accurate effects yield trustworthy Q, I-squared, and tau-squared.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when variance derivations are uncertain.
edges.example: Effect-variance pairs feeding tau-squared estimation.
edges.resolution_rule: Compute heterogeneity only from validated effect-variance pairs.

edges.why_related: The model decision determines whether weights include a tau-squared component.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Weighting consistent with the model yields valid pooling.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension between efficient and robust weighting under sparse data.
edges.example: Random-effects implying tau-squared-adjusted inverse-variance weights.
edges.resolution_rule: Weighting scheme follows from the justified model decision.

edges.why_related: The tau-squared estimate enters random-effects weight computation.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Correct tau-squared yields correct between-study weighting.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when tau-squared is unstable with few studies.
edges.example: DerSimonian-Laird tau-squared feeding the weight vector.
edges.resolution_rule: Use the estimator declared in the model decision for weights.

edges.why_related: The weight vector and effects are combined to compute the pooled estimate.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Valid weights produce an efficient, interpretable pooled effect.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when small studies gain disproportionate weight.
edges.example: Inverse-variance weights summing to the pooled mean.
edges.resolution_rule: Pooled estimate uses the documented weight vector.

edges.why_related: Heterogeneity (tau-squared) widens the confidence interval of the pooled estimate.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Incorporating tau-squared yields honest interval coverage.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when heterogeneity is so high pooling is questionable.
edges.example: tau-squared widening the random-effects CI.
edges.resolution_rule: If heterogeneity is extreme, prefer describing over pooling.

edges.why_related: The pooled estimate and per-study effects are what the forest plot displays.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Faithful plotting makes the synthesis auditable.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Minor tension over visual emphasis of the diamond.
edges.example: Diamond and prediction interval drawn from the pooled result.
edges.resolution_rule: Plot must show heterogeneity, not only the pooled diamond.

edges.why_related: Heterogeneity statistics change what the forest plot must communicate (prediction interval).
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Showing the prediction interval prevents overconfident reading.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension between a clean figure and full disclosure.
edges.example: Adding a prediction-interval bar when tau-squared is non-trivial.
edges.resolution_rule: Disclosure of heterogeneity dominates figure simplicity.

edges.why_related: Detected heterogeneity motivates and conditions subgroup investigation.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Subgroups can localize and explain heterogeneity.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension from multiplicity when many subgroups are tested.
edges.example: High I-squared prompting a planned subgroup split.
edges.resolution_rule: Investigate only pre-specified subgroups first to control multiplicity.

edges.why_related: Residual heterogeneity is the variance meta-regression covariates attempt to explain.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Meta-regression can attribute heterogeneity to study-level covariates.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension from overfitting with few studies.
edges.example: Regressing effect on baseline risk to explain tau-squared.
edges.resolution_rule: Require a minimum studies-per-covariate ratio before regressing.

edges.why_related: Subgroup analysis needs the moderator variables coded during extraction.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Coded moderators enable valid subgroup definition.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when moderators were not consistently reported.
edges.example: Extracted study-region variable defining a subgroup.
edges.resolution_rule: Only use moderators coded uniformly across studies.

edges.why_related: Meta-regression covariates come from study-level data captured at extraction.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Well-coded covariates support credible regression.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when covariates are missing for many studies.
edges.example: Mean baseline severity coded per study as a covariate.
edges.resolution_rule: Drop covariates with excessive missingness rather than impute blindly.

edges.why_related: The pooled estimate and per-study precision anchor the funnel plot.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Funnel diagnosis contextualizes the pooled effect.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension with few studies making the funnel unreliable.
edges.example: Funnel centered on the pooled effect with study precision on the y-axis.
edges.resolution_rule: Skip the funnel below ten studies and state the limitation.

edges.why_related: Visual funnel inspection precedes and motivates formal asymmetry testing.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Visual then formal layering avoids over-reading either alone.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when visual and formal results disagree.
edges.example: Asymmetric funnel triggering an Egger regression.
edges.resolution_rule: Formal tests interpreted alongside, not instead of, the funnel.

edges.why_related: Evidence of publication bias is a GRADE domain that can downgrade certainty.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Bias bounds feed an honest certainty rating.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when correction methods disagree on the bias magnitude.
edges.example: Strong small-study effects downgrading certainty one level.
edges.resolution_rule: Use the bias range, not a single corrected point, to inform grading.

edges.why_related: Sensitivity analysis perturbs the inputs and model behind the pooled estimate.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Robustness checks confirm the headline result is not an artifact.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension between thoroughness and specification fishing.
edges.example: Re-pooling under REML vs DL to test estimator sensitivity.
edges.resolution_rule: Pre-plan the sensitivity grid; report all specifications run.

edges.why_related: Influence diagnostics evaluate each study's leverage on the pooled estimate.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Detecting influential studies prevents single-trial-driven conclusions.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension over whether to remove an influential study.
edges.example: Leave-one-out re-estimation of the pooled effect.
edges.resolution_rule: Removal requires a documented methodological justification.

edges.why_related: The weighting scheme determines how much each study can influence the result.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Understanding weights explains observed influence.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Mild tension when robust weighting changes which study is influential.
edges.example: A heavily weighted large trial showing high Cook's distance.
edges.resolution_rule: Interpret influence relative to the declared weighting scheme.

edges.why_related: Influence diagnostics and broad sensitivity analysis are complementary robustness lenses.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Together they cover study-level and specification-level robustness.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Overlap risk of double-counting robustness claims.
edges.example: Leave-one-out (influence) plus estimator variation (sensitivity).
edges.resolution_rule: Report them as distinct robustness facets, not redundant checks.

edges.why_related: Comparable per-comparison effect sizes are required to build a treatment network.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Consistent effects enable valid direct and indirect synthesis.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when comparisons use heterogeneous outcome metrics.
edges.example: Pairwise log-ORs forming the network edges.
edges.resolution_rule: Harmonize the effect metric across all comparisons first.

edges.why_related: Between-study heterogeneity conditions the transitivity assumption a network requires.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Assessing heterogeneity supports a defensible transitivity judgment.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when heterogeneity undermines indirect comparison validity.
edges.example: Effect modifiers differing across the network compromising transitivity.
edges.resolution_rule: Do not rank treatments if transitivity is implausible.

edges.why_related: IPD synthesis needs the individual datasets identified and requested during the review.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Linking studies to their IPD enables individual-level modeling.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension from partial data availability.
edges.example: Requesting raw participant files for each eligible trial.
edges.resolution_rule: Document non-availability and assess availability bias.

edges.why_related: Aggregate effect-size and IPD approaches estimate related quantities by different means.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Two-stage IPD reduces to aggregate effects, aiding cross-checking.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Risk of conflating within- and across-study effects.
edges.example: Two-stage IPD per-study estimates matching aggregate effect sizes.
edges.resolution_rule: Keep within-study and across-study effects explicitly separate.

edges.why_related: Risk-of-bias judgments define a key sensitivity stratum (exclude high-risk studies).
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Quality-stratified sensitivity tests robustness to flawed studies.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when excluding high-risk studies removes most evidence.
edges.example: Re-pooling with only low-risk trials.
edges.resolution_rule: Report both full and low-risk-only estimates.

edges.why_related: Aggregate risk of bias across studies is a GRADE downgrading domain.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Bias judgments propagate into a defensible certainty rating.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when most weight comes from high-risk studies.
edges.example: Serious risk of bias downgrading certainty.
edges.resolution_rule: Downgrade certainty when high-risk studies dominate the pool.

edges.why_related: The pooled estimate and its precision feed the imprecision domain of GRADE.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Effect magnitude and CI width inform certainty.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when a significant effect has wide intervals.
edges.example: A wide CI crossing a decision threshold downgrading for imprecision.
edges.resolution_rule: Grade certainty from the interval, not the point estimate alone.

edges.why_related: Unexplained heterogeneity is the inconsistency domain of GRADE.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Quantified heterogeneity supports an inconsistency judgment.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when heterogeneity is real but unexplained.
edges.example: High tau-squared with no explanatory moderator downgrading certainty.
edges.resolution_rule: Downgrade for inconsistency when heterogeneity is unexplained.

edges.why_related: The current pooled estimate is the baseline updated as new studies accrue.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Cumulative ordering shows when conclusions stabilized.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension from repeated significance testing over time.
edges.example: Adding the newest trial to the running pooled estimate.
edges.resolution_rule: Apply sequential adjustment before claiming a new crossing is decisive.

edges.why_related: Final figures are artifacts the reproducible package must regenerate from code.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Script-generated figures guarantee reproducibility.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Minor tension with hand-edited graphics.
edges.example: Forest plot produced by the archived metafor script.
edges.resolution_rule: All figures must be regenerable from the packaged code.

edges.why_related: The sensitivity grid and its results must be captured in the reproducible package.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Archived specifications let others re-run robustness checks.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension with the effort of scripting every specification.
edges.example: All sensitivity specifications encoded in the analysis script.
edges.resolution_rule: Package every reported specification, not just the headline one.

edges.why_related: GRADE judgments and summary-of-findings tables belong in the final reporting package.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Logged grading rationale makes certainty claims auditable.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Minor tension with subjective grading documentation.
edges.example: Summary-of-findings table archived with downgrade rationale.
edges.resolution_rule: Each grading decision is recorded with its rationale in the package.

edges.why_related: The model choice constrains the inference method (z vs t, HKSJ) for the pooled CI.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Consistent inference method yields valid interval coverage.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when few-study CIs need Knapp-Hartung widening.
edges.example: Random-effects with Knapp-Hartung producing a wider CI.
edges.resolution_rule: Apply the inference method implied by the model and study count.

edges.why_related: The protocol's outcome hierarchy determines which outcomes are graded.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Pre-specified outcomes anchor the summary-of-findings table.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension when an unplanned outcome seems important to grade.
edges.example: Grading only the protocol's primary and key secondary outcomes.
edges.resolution_rule: Grade pre-specified outcomes; add others only with an amendment.

edges.why_related: The chosen model dictates which tau-squared estimator and reporting are appropriate.
edges.benefit_of_coupling: Aligned estimator choice keeps heterogeneity reporting coherent.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Tension between estimator simplicity and accuracy.
edges.example: Random-effects model implying REML tau-squared reporting.
edges.resolution_rule: Heterogeneity estimator follows the declared model.

conflict_axes.trigger: between-study heterogeneity is non-trivial but a tighter fixed-effect CI is tempting
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Inference target dominates: if generalizing beyond included studies, random-effects wins despite wider CIs.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: fixed-effect chosen with I-squared above 50% without justification
conflict_axes.example: Choosing random-effects for a heterogeneous drug-class meta-analysis intended to guide general practice.

conflict_axes.trigger: heterogeneity is so large a single pooled mean may mislead
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Validity dominates convenience: if the prediction interval spans clinically opposite effects, prefer narrative/structured description over a headline pooled number.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: prediction interval crosses the null and includes harmful and beneficial effects
conflict_axes.example: Declining to report a single pooled OR when effects range from strong benefit to harm.

conflict_axes.trigger: an unplanned subgroup or covariate shows a striking signal
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Pre-specification dominates: post-hoc findings are labeled exploratory and hypothesis-generating, never confirmatory.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a post-hoc subgroup difference is presented as a primary conclusion
conflict_axes.example: Reporting a striking unplanned age interaction only as exploratory.

conflict_axes.trigger: including all eligible studies pulls in many high-risk-of-bias trials
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Report the inclusive estimate but let risk-of-bias-stratified sensitivity determine the trusted conclusion.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the pooled estimate is driven mainly by high-risk studies
conflict_axes.example: Presenting all-studies and low-risk-only estimates side by side.

conflict_axes.trigger: asymmetry suggests bias but correction methods disagree
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Report the observed estimate plus a bias-adjusted range from multiple methods; never substitute one corrected point for the result.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a single trim-and-fill estimate is reported as the corrected truth
conflict_axes.example: Bounding the effect with both p-curve and a selection model rather than one correction.

conflict_axes.trigger: many candidate covariates compete to explain heterogeneity with few studies
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Parsimony dominates: enforce a minimum studies-per-covariate ratio and permutation testing before claiming explained variance.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: more covariates than the studies-per-covariate rule allows
conflict_axes.example: Limiting a 12-study regression to a single pre-specified covariate.

conflict_axes.trigger: a clean diamond reads as more certain than the dispersion warrants
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Disclosure dominates aesthetics: always display the prediction interval and heterogeneity statistics alongside the pooled diamond.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a forest plot omits the prediction interval despite non-trivial tau-squared
conflict_axes.example: Adding a prediction-interval bar beneath the pooled diamond.

conflict_axes.trigger: stakeholders want a clean treatment ranking from a sparse, possibly incoherent network
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Coherence dominates ranking appeal: do not publish SUCRA rankings unless transitivity and consistency are defensible.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: node-splitting reveals material inconsistency yet a ranking is requested
conflict_axes.example: Withholding a treatment ranking until inconsistency is resolved.

conflict_axes.trigger: deadline pressure tempts shipping results without a re-runnable package
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Reproducibility dominates: results are not final until they can be regenerated from archived data and code.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: results are released without code, data, or model specifications
conflict_axes.example: Holding publication until the metafor script reproduces every figure.

edge_cases.trigger: continuous and binary outcomes pooled without a common metric
edge_cases.failure_mode: meaningless pooled estimate from mixed effect-size scales
edge_cases.example: averaging an OR with an SMD
edge_cases.detection_method: check that all per-study effects share one declared metric and variance formula
resolution: convert all studies to one metric (e.g., SMD or log-OR)

edge_cases.trigger: fixed-effect model used with high I-squared
edge_cases.failure_mode: overstated precision and a spuriously narrow CI
edge_cases.example: reporting a fixed-effect CI with I-squared of 80%
edge_cases.detection_method: flag fixed-effect when I-squared exceeds the pre-set threshold without justification
resolution: switch to random-effects or justify fixed-effect against inference target

edge_cases.trigger: I-squared interpreted as the amount of heterogeneity
edge_cases.failure_mode: heterogeneity magnitude misjudged, prediction interval ignored
edge_cases.example: calling I-squared of 30% 'low heterogeneity' in a 4-study analysis
edge_cases.detection_method: require tau-squared and a prediction interval wherever I-squared is reported
resolution: interpret I-squared as proportion of variance, not amount

edge_cases.trigger: funnel/Egger applied with fewer than ten studies
edge_cases.failure_mode: false or missed publication-bias claim from an underpowered test
edge_cases.detection_method: block formal asymmetry tests below the minimum-studies threshold
resolution: defer formal testing until enough studies

edge_cases.trigger: many post-hoc subgroups tested until one is significant
edge_cases.failure_mode: false-positive subgroup effect presented as real
edge_cases.example: reporting the one significant split out of fifteen
edge_cases.detection_method: compare reported subgroups against the protocol's pre-specified list

edge_cases.trigger: an influential study removed without methodological justification
edge_cases.failure_mode: biased pooled estimate from convenience trimming
edge_cases.example: dropping the only null trial as an outlier
edge_cases.detection_method: require a logged rationale for any study exclusion at analysis stage

edge_cases.trigger: indirect comparisons pooled despite differing effect modifiers
edge_cases.failure_mode: invalid treatment ranking from violated transitivity
edge_cases.example: a SUCRA ranking driven by a non-transitive indirect loop
edge_cases.detection_method: assess effect-modifier distribution and run node-splitting before ranking

edge_cases.trigger: only a non-random subset of trials share individual data
edge_cases.failure_mode: availability bias in the IPD synthesis
edge_cases.detection_method: compare IPD-contributing studies to the full eligible set on key characteristics

edge_cases.example: continuity-correcting a zero-event arm distorts the OR
edge_cases.detection_method: scan effect inputs for zero cells and rare-event structure
resolution: use Mantel-Haenszel or Peto for rare events

edge_cases.trigger: significance retested at each new study in a living review
edge_cases.failure_mode: inflated type-I error from multiple looks
edge_cases.example: claiming significance the first time the CI excludes null
edge_cases.detection_method: check for sequential-monitoring adjustment in cumulative analyses

edge_cases.trigger: published estimate cannot be regenerated from archived materials
edge_cases.example: hand-edited figure differing from script output
edge_cases.detection_method: re-run the archived script and diff outputs against reported results

edge_cases.trigger: missing SDs imputed from p-values or CIs with wrong assumptions
edge_cases.failure_mode: distorted variances biasing weights and the pooled CI
edge_cases.example: deriving SD from a one-sided p-value misread as two-sided
edge_cases.detection_method: flag effect sizes whose variance came from imputation and check the assumption

workflow.objective: Fix the question and pre-register the protocol and planned models.
acceptance_tests: every planned outcome and model is documented
protocol is timestamped
exit_criteria: protocol exists and is locked against silent change
workflow.do_first_because: Pre-specification prevents data-driven model and outcome selection that inflates false positives.

workflow.objective: Search, screen, extract, and appraise the study base reproducibly.
acceptance_tests: inter-rater agreement meets threshold
every included study has a RoB judgment
exit_criteria: coded dataset and PRISMA flow complete
workflow.do_first_because: Bias introduced during retrieval and extraction cannot be fixed by any downstream model.

workflow.objective: Compute comparable, bias-corrected effect sizes and variances per study.
acceptance_tests: each effect has a correctly signed finite variance
small-sample correction applied where needed
workflow.do_first_because: All later modeling depends on comparable effects; errors here propagate everywhere.

workflow.objective: Choose the model, estimate heterogeneity, and set the weighting scheme.
acceptance_tests: heterogeneity reported with tau-squared and prediction interval
weights consistent with model
exit_criteria: model and heterogeneity locked for pooling
workflow.do_first_because: Model and heterogeneity decisions condition the pooled estimate and all robustness work.

workflow.objective: Compute the pooled estimate with correct inference and present it faithfully.
acceptance_tests: pooled CI uses the model-implied inference method
forest plot shows heterogeneity
workflow.do_first_because: The pooled estimate is the central result other diagnostics test and grading consumes.

workflow.objective: Diagnose small-study effects and bound publication-bias impact.
entry_criteria: ten or more studies for formal tests
gates: at least two complementary bias methods if testing
acceptance_tests: bias is reported as a bounded range, not a single corrected point
workflow.do_first_because: Publication-bias bounds are needed before certainty can be graded.

workflow.objective: Test robustness and investigate sources of heterogeneity.
acceptance_tests: conclusion robustness stated
exploratory analyses labeled as such
workflow.do_first_because: Robustness and moderator analyses qualify the headline result before grading.

workflow.objective: Grade certainty and run any advanced syntheses with their own assumption checks.
acceptance_tests: each certainty decision logged with rationale
advanced assumptions validated
exit_criteria: certainty graded and advanced analyses validated
workflow.do_first_because: Certainty and advanced methods carry the highest interpretation risk and need review before finalization.

workflow.objective: Bundle data, code, specifications, and PRISMA reporting into a re-runnable package.
entry_criteria: all analyses validated and certainty graded
gates: script regenerates all reported figures and estimates
acceptance_tests: independent re-run reproduces the pooled estimate
reporting checklist complete
workflow.do_first_because: A re-runnable package is the final gate that makes every analytic choice auditable and updatable.

priority_rationale.notes: Protocol gates every downstream choice; pre-specification controls false positives.
Retrieval bias is uncorrectable later, so completeness comes first.
Extracted data is the substrate for all effect computation.
Appraising quality early enables quality-aware synthesis and grading.
Comparable effects are the precondition for any pooling.
Model choice drives precision claims and downstream inference.
Heterogeneity conditions weighting, pooling, subgroups, networks, and grading.
Weights follow the model and heterogeneity and feed pooling.
The pooled estimate is the central result all diagnostics test.
The forest plot makes the result and its dispersion auditable.
Bias diagnosis precedes formal testing and grading.
Bias bounds are needed before certainty grading.
Robustness checks confirm the result is not a specification artifact.
Influence diagnostics reveal single-study-driven conclusions.
Pre-specified subgroups explain heterogeneity with controlled multiplicity.
Meta-regression attributes heterogeneity to covariates when studies suffice.
Grading consumes bias, heterogeneity, and risk-of-bias assessments.
Network synthesis is high-complexity and assumption-laden.
IPD is high-effort and prone to availability bias.
Cumulative/living updates require multiplicity control over time.
Reproducible packaging is the final auditability and update gate.

dominance_rules.trigger: heterogeneity makes a fixed-effect CI tempting
dominance_rules.rule: Match the model to the inference target even if it widens the interval.
dominance_rules.required_action: Use random-effects when generalizing beyond included studies and report sensitivity to the model.
dominance_rules.example: Choosing random-effects despite a tighter fixed-effect CI.

dominance_rules.trigger: an unplanned subgroup or covariate is significant
dominance_rules.rule: Confirmatory claims require pre-specification; post-hoc findings are exploratory.
dominance_rules.required_action: Label unplanned analyses exploratory and apply multiplicity adjustment.
dominance_rules.example: Reporting an unplanned interaction only as hypothesis-generating.

dominance_rules.rule: Always disclose heterogeneity and the prediction interval.
dominance_rules.required_action: Add the prediction interval and heterogeneity statistics to the forest plot.
dominance_rules.example: Drawing a prediction-interval bar under the pooled diamond.

dominance_rules.trigger: deadline pressure tempts skipping robustness or grading
dominance_rules.required_action: Complete bias, robustness, and certainty steps before release.
dominance_rules.example: Delaying release until sensitivity analyses are done.

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value step lacks its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: Do not finalize a step before its prerequisites are validated.
dominance_rules.required_action: Re-sequence so effect computation precedes pooling and grading.
dominance_rules.example: Refusing to grade certainty before pooling and bias assessment.

dominance_rules.trigger: a heuristic estimate is dressed as observed
dominance_rules.rule: Evidence labels and provenance dominate decimal precision.
dominance_rules.required_action: Keep all estimates labeled heuristic absent eligible observed data.
dominance_rules.example: Reporting tau-squared as heuristic, not measured fact.

dominance_rules.trigger: analysis is ready to finalize but checks are incomplete
dominance_rules.rule: Validation and acceptance tests must pass before any lock.
dominance_rules.required_action: Run reproducibility and consistency checks before hard lock.
dominance_rules.example: Blocking hard lock until the script reproduces the result.

dominance_rules.rule: High-risk grading and advanced-synthesis decisions require human review.
dominance_rules.required_action: Escalate certainty grading and network ranking to a methodologist.
dominance_rules.example: Routing a SUCRA ranking through expert review before publication.

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds what the evidence supports
dominance_rules.rule: Conclusions must not exceed the grounded, graded evidence.
dominance_rules.required_action: Downgrade or qualify any claim beyond the certainty rating.
dominance_rules.example: Stating 'moderate certainty' rather than 'proven' for a downgraded effect.

dominance_rules.trigger: stakeholders demand a ranking from an incoherent network
dominance_rules.rule: Do not publish rankings when transitivity or consistency fail.
dominance_rules.required_action: Withhold SUCRA until node-splitting shows acceptable coherence.
dominance_rules.example: Reporting only pairwise estimates when the network is incoherent.

dominance_rules.trigger: results are ready but not yet re-runnable
dominance_rules.rule: Results are not final until reproducible from archived data and code.
dominance_rules.required_action: Package and verify re-run before declaring results final.
dominance_rules.example: Holding sign-off until an independent re-run matches.

dominance_rules.trigger: a tempting shortcut creates a circular dependency
dominance_rules.rule: Preserve an acyclic dependency order over convenient shortcuts.
dominance_rules.required_action: Convert the weaker link to a sequence or feedback edge.
dominance_rules.example: Treating heterogeneity-to-model feedback as a feedback edge, not a cycle.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not extract data before the protocol is registered.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Locking the question first prevents data-driven scope and outcome drift.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: extraction begins with no timestamped protocol
anti_rework_rules.example: registering on PROSPERO before opening full texts.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not screen before the search strategy is documented and complete.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Screening an incomplete pool forces re-screening when the search is revised.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: screening starts before the search log is finalized
anti_rework_rules.example: finishing all database searches before title screening.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select the model before effect sizes are computed.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: The spread of effects informs the model decision.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a model is fixed before any effect is computed
anti_rework_rules.example: inspecting effect scatter before choosing random-effects.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not pool before heterogeneity is estimated.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Pooling without tau-squared yields wrong interval coverage.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a pooled CI is reported with no heterogeneity statistic
anti_rework_rules.example: computing tau-squared before the random-effects CI.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize weights before the model and tau-squared are set.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Weights depend on the model and tau-squared; premature weights need redoing.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: weights computed before the model decision is logged
anti_rework_rules.example: deriving random-effects weights only after tau-squared is fixed.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not grade certainty before bias and heterogeneity are assessed.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: GRADE domains require completed bias and inconsistency assessments.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a certainty rating is issued before bias testing
anti_rework_rules.example: finishing funnel and Egger work before grading.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not produce a network ranking before checking transitivity and consistency.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Rankings from incoherent networks are invalid and must be retracted.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a SUCRA ranking appears with no consistency check

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not present subgroups as confirmatory before checking the protocol list.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Post-hoc confirmatory claims must be relabeled, avoiding correction churn.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an unplanned subgroup is reported as a primary finding
anti_rework_rules.example: tagging only pre-specified subgroups as confirmatory.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not hard-lock results before acceptance and reproducibility tests pass.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Locking before tests forces version increments to fix defects.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a result is hard-locked with failing reproduction
anti_rework_rules.example: verifying the re-run reproduces the estimate before sign-off.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize high-risk grading or rankings before human review.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Irreversible interpretive claims need expert sign-off.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: certainty or a ranking is published without review
anti_rework_rules.example: routing the summary-of-findings through a methodologist first.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Update the validation report after every material analysis repair.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Untracked repairs break traceability and reproducibility.
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an analysis change leaves the validation record stale
anti_rework_rules.example: logging a re-pooling fix in the validation report.

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validation or acceptance test fails
iteration_protocol.detection: validator report shows a failed check
acceptance_tests: all failed checks enumerated

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and downstream impact
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect is first

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace affected edges and downstream nodes
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to its repair subsystem
action: route to subsystem (effects, model, bias, etc.)
acceptance_tests: each defect has an owner
previously failed checks now pass

iteration_protocol.detection: recompute posterior importance and revisit pressure
action: update priors and recompute derived scores
acceptance_tests: posterior change exceeds revisit delta where expected

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or bad reference is found
action: convert weaker dependency to sequence/feedback or fix reference
acceptance_tests: graph is acyclic and all references resolve
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycle or bad reference remains

acceptance_tests: downgrade and impact analysis recorded

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk above threshold or methods disagree
action: escalate to human reviewer with decision record
acceptance_tests: reviewer decision logged

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare counts and scores against the prior version
acceptance_tests: no unexplained regression in checks or counts

mandatory_checks: no observed labels without observed data

expected_properties: effect sizes converted to one metric

test_cases.input_summary: asymmetric funnel with many small studies

increment when a graded conclusion changes
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade to draft before editing a locked artifact
